images.title: The side of a square of area 64
images.purpose: Shows a square of area 64 square cm made of 64 unit cells, with each side 8 cm, the positive square root of 64.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. One large square in the centre with its two side lengths labelled and one equation below.
images.exact_structure: One large square filled light teal (#0072B2) with a dark outline, divided by thin grey (#6B7280) lines into an 8 by 8 grid of equal cells, 64 cells in all. The label 64 sq cm sits on a white tag in the centre. The bottom side is labelled 8 cm and the left side is labelled 8 cm, both in reddish purple (#CC79A7) with the sides drawn thicker in reddish purple. Below the square, centred: √64 = 8. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: The side of a square is the positive square root of its area.
images.description: Shows a square of area 64 square cm made of 64 unit cells, with each side 8 cm, the positive square root of 64.
images.context: Square roots of 64 are 8 and −8; a side uses the positive root.

image_decisions.why: Reading a side off a square of known area is the concrete meaning of a square root.
